fatal_errors: The proposed FeMnCoCrNi alloy is not the target AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA with coupled FCC and B2 phases.
The HPHT treatment at 5 GPa and 1000°C is unsupported and does not reconstruct the intermediate-temperature aging intervention.
The proposed 200-400°C transition window conflicts with the observed approximately 550-750°C window and the ductility minimum near 600°C.
The grain-refinement and homogeneous-microstructure mechanism omits the essential enhanced L12 ordering, elevated antiphase-boundary energy, planar slip, and jagged FCC/B2 phase-boundary effects.
Suppression of embrittlement and enhanced ductility does not mechanistically explain a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
The claimed 30% ductility increase and numerical falsification threshold have no cited evidentiary basis.
explanation: The hypothesis only aligns at the broad level of proposing a high-entropy alloy and claiming a ductile-brittle-ductile response. It misses the alloy identity, dual-phase starting structure, aging temperatures, brittle-window boundaries, structural mediators, and measured outcome. Its mechanism predicts generalized resistance to embrittlement rather than the target plastic instability caused by maximal L12 ordering and jagged FCC/B2 boundaries at 600°C, followed by recovery at 750°C. The proposed experiment could assess impact behavior and microstructure, but it lacks temperature-resolved aging controls and measurements capable of distinguishing ordering and phase-boundary-mediated cracking from impurity-segregation mechanisms. With no supporting evidence and several invented quantitative claims, it is an unsupported alternative rather than a reconstruction.
